business_model.claim: Ryder System, Inc. provides outsourced logistics and transportation services across North America through Fleet Management Solutions (FMS), Supply Chain Solutions (SCS), and Dedicated Transportation Solutions (DTS).
quotes: Ryder System, Inc. (Ryder) is a leading provider of outsourced logistics and transportation services throughout North America.

We report our financial performance based on three business segments: (1) Fleet Management Solutions (FMS), which provides full service leasing, commercial rental and vehicle maintenance services; (2) Supply Chain Solutions (SCS), which provides fully integrated logistics solutions; and (3) Dedicated Transportation Solutions (DTS), which provides turnkey transportation solutions, including dedicated vehicles, professional drivers, management and administrative support.

Among our services and product offerings, demand for used vehicles, rental and contractual sales are particularly susceptible to changes in economic and market conditions.
Rental power fleet utilization remained consistent at 70% compared to prior year.

business_model.claim: Cost of services (7,129 in 2025 and 5,596 in 2026 year-to-date through September, tables in millions) is driven by employee salaries, subcontracted transportation, fuel, lease expense, self-insured claims, and maintenance, including new-business ramp-up costs in SCS.
quotes: Cost of services represents the direct costs related to services revenue and is primarily comprised of salaries and employee-related costs, subcontracted transportation (purchased transportation from third parties), fuel, lease expense, insurance and maintenance costs.
Cost of services increased slightly more than revenue for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, primarily due to costs incurred to ramp up new business in SCS.
We are substantially self-insured for vehicle liability and workers' compensation claims.

Net gains on used vehicle sales increased in the third quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026, primarily due to higher pricing and an improved retail sales volume mix.
In addition, we remain on track to deliver over $70 million in expected earnings benefits from strategic initiatives this year, and are well positioned for continued growth.

We primarily sell our used vehicles through our retail channel, which allows us to leverage our maintenance expertise and strong brand reputation, and to realize higher sales proceeds than in the wholesale market.

As supply chains continue to expand and become more complex, the demand for outsourced logistics is expected to continue increasing as companies will require more sophisticated, cost-effective and reliable supply chain practices.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1 and Item 1A.
competitive_position.claim: Ryder faces intense competition across all markets from customer self-performance, competitors with greater capital resources or lower cost structures, new entrants with lower costs or stronger technology, multi-carrier bidding, and trucking consolidation.
quotes: The transportation and logistics industry is highly competitive.

Increased competition or our inability to compete successfully may lead to a reduction in revenues, reduced profit margins, increased pricing pressure or a loss of market share, any one of which could affect our financial results.
As an alternative to using our services, customers may choose to provide these services themselves or obtain similar services from other third parties.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1.
competitive_position.claim: In FMS specifically, Ryder competes with finance lessors, truck and trailer manufacturers, independent dealers, and managed maintenance providers that coordinate independent repair networks.
quotes: We compete with finance lessors, truck and trailer manufacturers and independent dealers.
We also face competition from managed maintenance providers who are hired to coordinate and manage the maintenance of large fleets through a network of independent maintenance providers.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A.
competitive_position.claim: Cost of capital is a significant competitive factor, so higher debt or equity costs from credit rating reductions or stock price volatility could impair Ryder's competitive position.
quotes: because cost of capital is a significant competitive factor, any increase in either the cost of our debt or equity as a result of, for example, reductions in our debt rating or stock price volatility could have a significant impact on our competitive position.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A and Item 7 and the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q Item 2.
competitive_position.claim: Because customer freight and fleet demand is cyclical, economic downturns, inflation, higher interest rates, tariffs, and trade policy changes can depress rental, used-vehicle, and contractual demand and leave excess capacity in SCS multi-client warehouses.
quotes: The transportation industry is highly cyclical and susceptible to trends in economic activity.
If customer demand is lower than expected we may have excess capacity in our warehouses.

While we are experiencing positive momentum in our businesses, inflationary cost pressures including higher fuel costs, regulatory changes, geopolitical events, labor interruptions, changes in tariff, trade or tax policies and the continued higher interest rate environment may negatively impact demand for our business, financial results and significant judgments and estimates.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1, Item 1A, and Item 7.
competitive_position.claim: Ryder retains vehicle residual risk on ChoiceLease, so falling used-vehicle market prices can cause losses on vehicle sales or higher depreciation, as occurred in 2025 when used truck and tractor pricing declined 15% and 11%, respectively.
quotes: In the past, we have realized losses on sales of used vehicles at the end of a vehicle's useful life when our residual value estimates were above used vehicle market prices due to rapidly changing market conditions.
Lower gains on used vehicles sales reflect a 15% and 11% decrease in used truck and tractor pricing, respectively.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A.
competitive_position.claim: Long-term SCS, DTS, ChoiceLease, and SelectCare contracts rely on assumptions for volumes, wages, labor availability, maintenance costs, inflation, and interest rates, and inability to reprice some customized SCS and DTS contracts can compress margins or cause lost business.
quotes: If we are incorrect in our operational assumptions, or, as a result of subsequent changes in customer demand or other market forces that are outside of our control, these assumptions prove to be invalid, we could have lower margins than anticipated in a contract or segment, lose business, or be unable to offer competitive products and services.
We may not be able to adjust the pricing terms in some of our SCS and DTS contracts in the event any of our assumptions prove to be invalid.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A.
competitive_position.claim: Because Ryder commits capital months in advance for its commercial rental fleet, forecasting errors can produce overcapacity—forcing lower pricing, higher depreciation, or disposal losses—or undercapacity that harms reliability and reputation.
quotes: We make commitments to purchase the vehicles months in advance of the expected use of the vehicle and seek to optimize the size and mix of the commercial rental fleet based on demand projections and various other factors.
Overcapacity could require us to deploy or sell vehicles at lower than anticipated pricing levels, which may result in higher depreciation or losses on vehicle sales.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A.
competitive_position.claim: Rapid technological changes—including zero-emission vehicles reducing diesel maintenance demand, autonomous or driver-assist vehicles, AI, and warehouse automation such as autonomous mobile robots—threaten service demand and require heavy capital investment that customers may not fund.
quotes: Certain innovations, such as an increase in customer use of zero-emission vehicles, for example, could reduce the demand for our diesel vehicle and related maintenance and other offerings.

If warehouse automation technologies reduce the number of warehouse associates needed at a facility, it could adversely affect our financial condition and operational results as it could decrease SCS revenue or lead to a decrease in demand for our services.

Moreover, advances in technology may require us to increase investments in order to remain competitive, and our customers may not be willing to accept higher prices to cover the cost of these investments.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A.
competitive_position.claim: SCS and DTS face substantial customer concentration and credit risk, as the top ten customers in each segment accounted for approximately one-third of each segment's total revenue and operating revenue in 2025.
quotes: During 2025, sales to our top ten customers in each of SCS and DTS accounted for approximately one-third of total revenue and operating revenue for each segment.

Although we maintain multiple service contracts with each of these large customers, the loss of or reduction in business from one or more of these large customers could have a material adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A.
competitive_position.claim: FMS relies on a relatively small number of vehicle OEMs and concentrated component suppliers, exposing fleet growth, parts availability, and brand reputation to supplier disruptions or broad-based recalls.
quotes: We buy vehicles and related equipment from a relatively small number of OEMs in our FMS business.
Some of our OEMs rely on a small concentration of suppliers for certain vehicle parts, components and equipment.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A.
competitive_position.claim: IT system outages, legacy consolidation or M&A integration challenges, third-party vendor breaches, and sophisticated cyberattacks or AI and data-privacy compliance failures could disrupt operations and cause reputational or competitive harm.
quotes: While we maintain an information security program that consists of industry standard safeguards and controls to help safeguard our confidential information, including security training and compliance protocols, we cannot prevent or mitigate all data breaches or cyber incidents.

We use artificial intelligence in our business, and challenges with its use could result in reputational or competitive harm and legal liability, which could have an adverse impact on our results of operations.

competitive_position.basis: Stated directly in the 2025 Form 10-K Item 1A.
competitive_position.claim: Failure to execute Ryder's balanced growth strategy, innovate in line with evolving customer needs, or integrate acquisitions and capture expected synergies could erode its competitive advantage and profitability.
quotes: Failure to execute our business strategy may negatively impact our ability to continue to create long-term shareholder value and may result in stock price volatility.

If we do not respond to current customer needs and establish new, and further develop existing, customer relationships, our ability to maintain a competitive advantage and continue to grow our business profitability could be negatively affected.

growth_thesis.claim: Ryder targets growth from secular trends toward outsourcing private commercial fleets and complex North American supply chain logistics, noting that of approximately 11 million U.S. commercial fleet vehicles, 5 million are privately owned, and of approximately $1.5 trillion in U.S. target-market logistics spending, $234 billion was outsourced.
quotes: We aim to achieve this by growing with existing customers and new prospects who internally manage their supply chain services.

We continue to benefit from favorable long-term secular trends in logistics and transportation solutions and have experienced strong contractual sales activity across all three of our business segments, with activity accelerating in FMS and DTS due to increasing demand for capacity from quality carriers.

growth_thesis.claim: For outsourcing-driven growth to continue, customers must choose Ryder over in-house operations or competing providers while macroeconomic conditions, trade policies, and customer goods demand support shipping and fleet volumes.

growth_thesis.claim: Contractual new business in SCS and ChoiceLease drove third-quarter 2026 total revenue up 8% to $3,433 (table in millions) and operating revenue up 6% to $2,759 (table in millions), with SCS operating revenue up 9% and ChoiceLease revenue up 4%, following record SCS sales in 2025.
quotes: In 2026, we are well positioned for growth in SCS as we achieved record sales in 2025.

Operating revenue (a non-GAAP measure excluding fuel and subcontracted transportation) increased 6% in the third quarter of 2026, and 3% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, reflecting contractual revenue growth in SCS and FMS, partially offset by lower DTS fleet count.
In FMS, pre-tax earnings as a percent of operating revenue rose to 13.2%, reflecting our high-quality lease portfolio and early benefits from the freight market recovery.

growth_thesis.claim: For contractual SCS and ChoiceLease growth to continue, Ryder must retain its concentrated large customer base—where the top ten customers in SCS and DTS each accounted for approximately one-third of segment revenue in 2025—control new-contract ramp-up costs, maintain warehouse utilization, and secure timely OEM vehicle supply.
quotes: During 2025, sales to our top ten customers in each of SCS and DTS accounted for approximately one-third of total revenue and operating revenue for each segment.
If customer demand is lower than expected we may have excess capacity in our warehouses.

growth_thesis.claim: Execution of strategic initiatives—focused on lease pricing, maintenance cost savings, acquisition synergies, and omnichannel network optimization—is on track to deliver over $70 million in expected earnings benefits in 2026.

Although these contracts include indexed price escalation clauses or permit renegotiation upon a material change, there is no assurance that we will be successful in obtaining the necessary price adjustments or that pricing will be sufficient to cover the risk.
